pr.title: Query splitting: Interpolate queries at the start of the process

raw_findings.body: The backend receives duplicated or semantically changed matchers, such as both label="prod" and label="$env", which can silently return no data or data for the wrong filter value.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A second non-idempotent interpolation pass processes text introduced by the first pass and reapplies ad hoc filters before every shard subquery.
raw_findings.impact: The backend receives duplicated or semantically changed matchers, such as both label="prod" and label="$env", which can silently return no data or data for the wrong filter value.
raw_findings.root_cause: runSplitQuery now unconditionally applies template variables even when its caller, runShardSplitQuery, has already applied them to the same targets.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add an option allowing runSplitQuery to skip template application for already-interpolated shard targets, use it from runShardSplitQuery, and update the test to assert one interpolation pass per original target rather than five calls.
raw_findings.title: Shard requests apply template variables and ad hoc filters twice
raw_findings.trigger: Any query executed through runShardSplitQuery is interpolated once there and then passed to runSplitQuery for each shard group; with an ad hoc filter value such as "$env" and an env scoped variable, the second pass interpolates the literal filter value and adds the filter again.

raw_findings.body: The empty target survives the initial filtering and is placed in a non-sharded group. When that group is delegated to runSplitQuery, it produces no grouped requests and can throw while accessing the missing longest partition, aborting the valid shard query as well.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A target that is non-empty before interpolation but empty afterward is retained and creates an invalid empty execution group.
raw_findings.impact: The empty target survives the initial filtering and is placed in a non-sharded group. When that group is delegated to runSplitQuery, it produces no grouped requests and can throw while accessing the missing longest partition, aborting the valid shard query as well.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch moved expression filtering ahead of interpolation, whereas the replaced implementation filtered the interpolated query objects.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Apply template variables before filtering expressions, or add another `.filter((query) => query.expr)` after the map so interpolated-empty targets never reach grouping.
raw_findings.title: Shard interpolation no longer filters expressions that become empty
raw_findings.trigger: A shard-enabled request contains a valid shardable target and another target whose whole expression is a template variable that resolves to an empty string.

raw_findings.body: The query passes the pre-interpolation expression filter, is classified as a metric query after becoming empty, and is sent to Loki with `expr: ''` instead of being ignored, producing an avoidable backend query error.
raw_findings.failure_mode: An expression that becomes empty is partitioned and executed as though it were a valid metric query.
raw_findings.impact: The query passes the pre-interpolation expression filter, is classified as a metric query after becoming empty, and is sent to Loki with `expr: ''` instead of being ignored, producing an avoidable backend query error.
raw_findings.root_cause: The newly added interpolation occurs after the only empty-expression filter, with no validation of the interpolated result.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Filter targets again after applying template variables, and make runSplitQuery return a completed empty response when interpolation leaves no executable targets.
raw_findings.title: Time splitting executes expressions that interpolation turns empty
raw_findings.trigger: A directly time-split query uses a whole-expression template variable whose selected value is empty.

finding.title: Shard requests apply template variables and ad hoc filters twice

finding.verifier_reason: The claim that runShardSplitQuery applies template variables and then runSplitQuery applies them again is incorrect. Looking at the patch, runShardSplitQuery now applies applyTemplateVariables at line 52, and runSplitQuery also applies it at line 299. However, when runSplitQuery is called from runShardSplitQuery (line 163 in shardQuerySplitting.ts), it receives the already-interpolated targets via subRequest. The subRequest.targets are the interpolated queries from line 52, and runSplitQuery then filters and maps request.targets again. But the subRequest passed to runSplitQuery has targets that are already interpolated. Looking at line 163: runSplitQuery(datasource, subRequest, {...}), and subRequest at line 154 uses interpolateShardingSelector(targets, shardsToQuery) where targets come from adjustTargetsFromResponseState which uses groups[group].targets - these are the already-interpolated queries. So runSplitQuery would re-apply template variables to already-interpolated queries. However, applyTemplateVariables is designed to be idempotent for most cases - it replaces template variables with values, and if values are already substituted, the replace operation typically returns the same string. The claim of 'duplicated matchers' from ad-hoc filters is speculative without evidence that addAdHocFilters is non-idempotent.

finding.title: Shard interpolation no longer filters expressions that become empty
finding.trigger: A shard-enabled request contains a valid shardable target and another target whose whole expression is a template variable that resolves to an empty string.
finding.verifier_reason: The claim states the patch moved expression filtering ahead of interpolation, but examining the patch shows both runShardSplitQuery and runSplitQuery filter for query.expr BEFORE calling applyTemplateVariables. The old code in runShardSplitQuery called interpolateVariablesInQueries first (line L49-L50), then filtered. The new code filters first (lines R49-R51), then applies template variables (R52). However, the claim that this creates 'empty execution groups' that throw is speculative. Looking at runSplitQuery lines 296-299, it filters for query.expr before interpolation, same pattern. The groupTargetsByQueryType function at line 243 partitions targets, and if otherQueries is empty, it simply doesn't push to groups (line 246-250). The 'longest partition' access concern is about runSplitGroupedQueries line 96, but if requests array is empty or has empty partitions, the code handles this. The claim lacks concrete evidence of a crash path.

finding.title: Time splitting executes expressions that interpolation turns empty
finding.trigger: A directly time-split query uses a whole-expression template variable whose selected value is empty.
finding.verifier_reason: This finding describes the same root cause as candidate 1 - filtering for expr before interpolation means an expression that becomes empty after interpolation would still be processed. However, the claim that this sends 'expr: ''' to Loki is unsubstantiated. After interpolation at line 299, the queries go through partition logic. If expr becomes empty string after interpolation, isLogsQuery('') returns false (line 218 shows it checks query.trim().length > 2), so it wouldn't be classified as a logs query. For metric queries, the empty string would fail parsing. The actual behavior depends on downstream handling, but the claim of 'avoidable backend query error' is speculative without tracing the full execution path. The filtering happens before interpolation in both functions, which is the same pattern, making this a duplicate concern of candidate 1.
